correctness.rationale: The derivative at disease-free zero is (1−δ)I+βA; a positive Perron subsolution gives existence exactly above βρ>δ, while the strict product union bound paired with a Perron left vector forbids positive fixed points at/below threshold. Coordinate monotonicity and strict ray sublinearity F(tp)≫tF(p) for 0<t<1 yield uniqueness. The equitable two-dimensional cell-constant subspace is invariant and contains a positive equilibrium from a lifted Perron seed; uniqueness forces the full equilibrium to be cell constant. Equal probabilities yield (1−βq)^{d1+b1}=(1−βq)^{d2+b2}, equivalent to equal full degrees; conversely equal degrees give a homogeneous positive fixed point. Connectedness of supercritical parameter domain, continuous positive equilibrium, and near-onset convergence to the quotient Perron eigenvector determine sign: for r=v1/v2 its equation b2 r²+(d2−d1)r−b1=0 is positive at r=1 exactly when full degree2>degree1. A 6-vertex C4 ∨ K2 with quotient [[2,2],[4,1]] has degree4 vs5 opposite internal degrees2 vs1, with rational strict sub/supersolutions at β=.3,δ=.4. Direct exact quotient and numerical fixed-point calculations agree. A three-cell quotient [[4,1,0],[1,2,1],[0,1,5]] has v2>v1 near onset although degree2<degree1.

originality.rationale: The discrete product-form SIS map and spectral threshold are established Chakrabarti et al. prior art; equitable quotient reduction for continuous-time NIMFA is also established. The present claim is the uniform across-parameter ordering by full degrees for exactly two equitable cells, a minimum six-vertex isolated-threshold inversion, and a sharp failure at three cells. Dung–Phuc 2026 describes local/global threshold comparisons in its accessible abstract, but its complete original text was not accessible this run (ResearchGate 429; arXiv HTML disabled), hence no whole-paper noncoverage claim. Continuous-time product-free dynamics are not equivalent without a proof transfer; originality remains qualified.
